interpretation: Original failure is reproducible; numerical method, timestep, or tiny timestamp rounding changes move/remove it without modifying circuit conditions.
Decimal rounding alone is insufficient: full rounded-trap run fails later around202ns.
Gear2 reaches829ns; short-window conduction and energy agree closely with successful fine-step Trap.
Evidence supports a numerical convergence issue around PWL slope changes; it does not identify a specific ngspice implementation defect.
Gear2 alone does not guarantee high-rate convergence. At1/2/4/8Gbps Gear2 plus reltol1e-5 and chgtol1e-16 completed all original durations without physical changes.
Higher-rate trials are named A{rate}-rel1e5-c1e16; A4 fine-step control uses maxstep1ps. Other trial names expose their sole option/source changes; exact decks are hashed.
B still needs many steps with Gear2; no claim that B step count is solely trapezoidal numerical ringing.
These diagnostic B results retain the earlier0.35um diffusion recipe and are not the final matched-geometry architecture comparison.
limitations: no optical bandwidth, measured BER, silicon or PEX claim
positive draw excludes actual regulator loss
